title: Canonical classical lisse restriction and finite inverse-pair interfaces
statement: Use the normalized classical lisse restriction model interfaces [def-zl-classical-lisse-restriction-models]. A supplied finite reduced locally closed partition [def-constructible-stratification; def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] of a finite-type geometric scheme carries chosen classical lisse systems, integral lattices at one finite coefficient field, their localization identifications, and realization identifications with restrictions of a fixed sf heart object [def-weil-constructible-heart; def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]. Define restriction realization by the finite normalized square and the canonical completed compositor [def-zl-weil-ind-sheaf-category]. For an ambient Weil map [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] and a Frobenius-commuting immersion define its actual restricted map by conjugation with the two completed compositors. A Weil lift consists of a rational classical isomorphism and its inverse realizing precisely this restricted pair. Its comparison with ordinary automorphism pullback [def-wf-lisse-adic-automorphism-pullback] is pinned on the actual finite quotient pullback units. Its finite representative is an inverse pair over one coefficient enlargement, on the diagram scalar extensions of the original pair objects, with canonical coefficient arrows identifying both represented maps. Successive and scalar restrictions use the same completed-system operations.
